title: Ultradilute quasi-two-dimensional Bose-Bose liquid mixtures
authors: Leandra Vranješ Markić, Ivan Poparić, Krešimir Dželalija, Petar Stipanović, Jordi Boronat
abstract: We study ultradilute $^{39}$K Bose-Bose bulk mixtures and droplets in an external harmonic potential that confines them in one spatial direction towards the two-dimensional (2D) limit. Equations of state for several confinements are obtained with quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) at $T=0$, using interaction potentials that include information on the $s$-wave scattering length $a$ and the effective range $r_{\rm eff}$. Performing the calculations using two different interaction potential models we have determined the range of confinements for which equations of state are universal in terms of $a$ and $r_{\rm eff}$. Based on the QMC equation of state, we develop a 2D QMC density functional for each confinement strength and use it together with the local density approximation to determine properties of the self-bound drops. For moderate squeezing, energies and droplet profiles obtained using the 2D QMC functional agree well with those obtained using 3D functionals, while offering a substantial reduction in computational cost, and a consistent approach in crossover to 2D. Noticeably, our results approach 2D mean-field (MF) + Lee-Huang-Yang (LHY) predictions only for the most strongly confined systems for which universality in terms of $a$ and $r_{\rm eff}$ is observed. This implies a very narrow range of confinements for which 2D LHY functionals are applicable, which has important consequences for the study of vortices.
summary: The research uses Quantum Monte Carlo simulations to model Bose-Bose liquid mixtures confined towards two dimensions. It rigorously tests theoretical functionals against these calculations, finding that while 2D models offer computational savings, they break down rapidly as confinement increases beyond a narrow regime. This work is vital for accurately predicting the behavior of quantum droplets and vortices in highly constrained atomic systems.
main_problem: The study investigates ultradilute Bose-Bose liquid mixtures confined towards the quasi-two-dimensional (2D) limit to determine the confinement regime where their equations of state exhibit universality.
main_result: QMC calculations show that universal descriptions based on two scattering parameters ($a$ and $r_{	ext{eff}}$) are only valid for moderate confinement, suggesting a very narrow range where 2D Lee-Huang-Yang (LHY) functionals are applicable.
method: The study employs Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods at zero temperature to calculate equations of state and develop density functionals, comparing these results against established LHY predictions.
model_or_system: The system is a mixture of $^{39}	ext{K}$ bosons confined in an external harmonic potential, allowing for the study of crossover from 3D bulk behavior towards ideal 2D physics.
key_observables: Equations of state, density profiles (with and without vortices), saturation densities, and droplet energies per particle ($E/N$).
important_parameters: Scattering length ($a$), effective range ($r_{	ext{eff}}$), and the confinement strength quantified by the harmonic oscillator length ($a_z$) or squeezing factor ($f$).
main_assumptions: The applicability of 2D LHY functionals is severely limited to a narrow range of confinement, and two scattering parameters are insufficient for describing interactions below a certain confinement threshold.
figures_summary: Figures compare energy per particle vs. density showing universality limits (Fig. 1); they also contrast droplet density profiles between QMC and LHY methods across varying confinements (Fig. 2), and show the departure of DMC results from LHY predictions as confinement increases (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper develops theoretical frameworks using QMC to calculate equations of state for various confinements, compares these rigorous results against simpler models like the 2D LHY functional, and applies this analysis to predict properties of self-bound quantum droplets.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial benchmarks for modeling strongly interacting ultracold atomic mixtures in quasi-low dimensional geometries, highlighting the limitations of mean-field approximations (like LHY) when full correlation effects are important.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Equation of state of the bulk phase for a magnetic field B = 56.337 G and several harmonic confinements de- scribed by the squeezing factor f = az/0.639 µm. The calcu- lations are performed for two different potential models with same scattering length and effective range, showing universal- ity up to f = 0.05. The liquid distribution in the direction of squeezing follows has the single-particle gaussian shape, which is shown in the inset. From wider, to narrower distributions correspond to f=0.25, 0.15, 0.05 and 0.01.

FIG. 3. The equilibrium densities of the bulk liquid, obtained with quasi-2D QMC calculations are compared to 2D LHY predictions following Ref. [11] and to saturation densities of droplets studied with DFT functionals, as a function of the harmonic oscillator length describing the quasi-2D confine- ment.
FIG. 2. Density profiles of droplets obtained with the 2D QMC and 2D LHY functionals compared for two different squeezings f=0.15 (top) and f = 0.05 (bottom), for the mag- netic field B = 56.337 G.

FIG. 4. Energy per particle of the droplets as a function of N −1/2 calculated with 2D and 3D QMC and LHY functionals, for three different squeezings. The dots at zero x axis correspond to the equilibrium energy in quasi-2D bulk DMC calculation. The insets show the cut through the 3D droplet profile at x = 0 for droplets of size N = 20000 and N = 5000 (for the strongest squeezing only). The z coordinate has been multiplied by a factor of 10 for clarity.

FIG. 5. Density profiles of droplets with 100000 atoms in a magnetic field B = 56.574 G with f = 0.25 and angular velocity Ω= 2π×10 Hz, without vortex (VF) and with vortex in both components (V12), calculated using different density functionals. Droplet with vortex calculated using 2D LHY functional is metastable.
